Methods for selector objects

selector-methods.Rd

The objects returned by the select_* functions support:

  • predict(): predictions on new data, using the selected model.

  • tidy(): a tibble with one row per candidate term.

  • coef(): the selected coefficients (including the intercept).

  • print(): a short summary of the selection.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'selector'
predict(object, newdata, ...)

# S3 method for class 'selector'
tidy(x, scale_coef = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'selector'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'selector'
coef(object, use_native = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object, x

a selector

newdata

a data frame to predict on

...

for coef(), passed to the native coef method when use_native = TRUE; otherwise not used

scale_coef

if TRUE (default), coefficients are per standard deviation of each predictor; if FALSE, per unit. See "Scale of the coefficients".

use_native

if TRUE, call the underlying fit's own coef method (e.g. coef.cv.glmnet) instead

Value

  • tidy(): a tibble with columns term (every candidate term, plus the intercept), selected (1 if the selector kept the term, else 0; the intercept is always 1) and coef (the selector's estimate, e.g. the penalized estimate for select_glmnet() or select_ncvreg(); 0 when not selected).

  • coef(): a named vector of the selected coefficients, including the intercept, always on the scaled metric.

  • predict(): a vector of predictions for newdata.

Scale of the coefficients

Before selection, every select_* function builds the model matrix as model.matrix() would (factors, logicals and character predictors are treatment-coded, so the columns are named e.g. g3mid, am1, fTRUE), then centers each column and divides it by its standard deviation, dummies included. The outcome is not transformed. So, by default (scale_coef = TRUE), a coefficient is the change in the outcome per standard deviation of that column. With scale_coef = FALSE, slopes are divided by the column's standard deviation, giving the usual per-unit change. The centers and standard deviations come from the data the selector was first fit to, and are reused by reselect() and predict().

The intercept is never unscaled: it is the predicted outcome (on the link scale) at the means of the predictors, not the intercept lm() would report on the raw data. (select_stepwise_ic() leaves dummies uncentered, so there it is the prediction at each factor's reference level.)

Ordered factors are not supported (convert them to numeric scores or unordered factors first), nor are missing values in the outcome or predictors.
